title: Encoded Gate Kind Walk
statement: Let $C$ be a family of Boolean circuits, and fix Boolean $\ell_m$ and natural numbers $n,i,B$. Suppose a gate $g$ occurs at index $V-n$ in the circuit for input length $n$, with $n\le V\le B$. If $k\le i$, $k+2\le B$, and $U,W\le B$, then the walk initialized in state $kA$ with registers $(k,V,U,W)$ and no result has the following behavior on the input encoding $n$ and $i$: for $k\le i<k+2$, it halts with answer $\ell_m$ or the corresponding bit of the two-bit encoding of $g$'s kind; for $k+2\le i$, it reaches the specified postcondition, with every register bounded by $B$ throughout the run before reaching it.
hypotheses_covered: $g$ occurs at index $V-n$ in the circuit for input length $n$
